functions.name: abs
functions.doc: Absolute value of X. NULL yields NULL; a string or blob that cannot be read as a number yields 0.0. Raises an integer overflow error for the most negative 64-bit integer.

functions.name: changes
functions.doc: Number of rows inserted, updated or deleted by the most recently completed INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE statement on this connection.

functions.name: char
functions.doc: Builds a string whose characters have the given Unicode code point values, in argument order.

functions.name: coalesce
functions.doc: Returns the first argument that is not NULL, or NULL if every argument is NULL. Requires at least two arguments; later arguments are not evaluated once a non-NULL value is found.

functions.name: concat
functions.doc: Joins the text form of all non-NULL arguments into one string. NULL arguments are skipped; if all are NULL the result is an empty string.

functions.name: concat_ws
functions.doc: Joins the non-NULL arguments after the first, placing SEP between each pair. Returns NULL if SEP is NULL; NULL values are skipped.

functions.name: format
functions.doc: Alias of printf(): renders FORMAT using C printf-style substitutions such as %d, %s, %f, %q, %Q, %w and %z, filling them from the remaining arguments.

functions.name: glob
functions.doc: Function form of the GLOB operator; note the pattern comes first: glob(P, S) equals S GLOB P. Case-sensitive, with * ? and [...] wildcards. Returns 1 or 0.

functions.name: hex
functions.doc: Treats X as a blob (numbers and text are first converted to their UTF-8 text bytes) and returns its contents as upper-case hexadecimal.

functions.name: ifnull
functions.doc: Returns X if it is not NULL, otherwise Y. Equivalent to coalesce() with exactly two arguments.

functions.name: iif

signatures.doc: Classic three-argument form.
3.48.0+: returns NULL when COND is false.
3.48.0+: any number of condition/value pairs, optional trailing ELSE; if() is an alias.

functions.doc: Inline conditional: returns THEN when COND is true, otherwise ELSE. Shorthand for CASE WHEN COND THEN THEN ELSE ELSE END; only the chosen branch is evaluated.

functions.name: instr
functions.doc: 1-based position of the first occurrence of Y inside X, or 0 if not found. Counts characters for text and bytes when both are blobs; NULL if either argument is NULL.

functions.name: last_insert_rowid
functions.doc: Rowid of the most recent successful INSERT into a rowid table on this database connection.

functions.name: length
functions.doc: Character count for text (up to the first NUL), byte count for blobs, length of the text rendering for numbers, and NULL for NULL.

functions.name: like

signatures.doc: With an escape character.

functions.doc: Function form of LIKE with the pattern first: like(P, S) equals S LIKE P, and like(P, S, E) adds ESCAPE E. % matches any run, _ one character; ASCII case-insensitive by default.

functions.name: likelihood
functions.doc: Returns X unchanged; tells the query planner that X is true with probability P (a constant from 0.0 to 1.0).

functions.name: likely
functions.doc: Returns X unchanged; a planner hint that X is usually true. Same as likelihood(X, 0.9375).

functions.name: load_extension

signatures.doc: With an explicit entry-point symbol.

functions.doc: Loads a shared-library extension from FILE, optionally using entry point ENTRY. Only works if extension loading has been enabled on the connection; returns NULL or raises an error.

functions.name: lower
functions.doc: Copy of X with ASCII letters converted to lower case. Non-ASCII case folding requires the ICU extension.

functions.name: ltrim

signatures.doc: Strips leading spaces.
Strips any leading characters found in CHARS.

functions.doc: Removes characters from the left end of X: spaces by default, or any character contained in CHARS.

functions.name: max

signatures.doc: Scalar: largest argument; NULL if any argument is NULL.
Aggregate: largest non-NULL value in the group.

functions.doc: With two or more arguments, a scalar returning the largest argument (NULL if any is NULL). With one argument, an aggregate returning the largest non-NULL value in the group, or NULL if none.

functions.name: min

signatures.doc: Scalar: smallest argument; NULL if any argument is NULL.
Aggregate: smallest non-NULL value in the group.

functions.doc: With two or more arguments, a scalar returning the smallest argument (NULL if any is NULL). With one argument, an aggregate returning the smallest non-NULL value in the group, or NULL if none.

functions.name: nullif
functions.doc: Returns NULL when X and Y are equal, otherwise returns X.

functions.name: octet_length
functions.doc: Number of bytes needed to store X: bytes of a blob, or bytes of the text form in the database encoding (UTF-8 or UTF-16). NULL for NULL.

functions.name: printf
functions.doc: Formats a string C-printf style from FORMAT and the following arguments. Supports %d %i %f %e %g %s %c %x %o plus SQLite extras %q %Q %w %z; same as format().

functions.name: quote
functions.doc: Renders X as an SQL literal: text in single quotes with inner quotes doubled, blobs as X'hex', numbers as-is, and NULL as the word NULL.

functions.name: random
functions.doc: Pseudo-random signed 64-bit integer spanning the full integer range.

functions.name: randomblob
functions.doc: Blob of N pseudo-random bytes (at least 1). Combine with hex() to generate random identifiers.

functions.name: replace
functions.doc: Replaces every occurrence of Y in X with Z, using binary comparison. If Y is empty, X is returned unchanged.

functions.name: round

signatures.doc: Rounds to zero decimal places.
Rounds to DIGITS places right of the decimal point.

functions.doc: Floating-point value of X rounded to DIGITS decimal places (default 0). Negative DIGITS is treated as 0.

functions.name: rtrim

signatures.doc: Strips trailing spaces.
Strips any trailing characters found in CHARS.

functions.doc: Removes characters from the right end of X: spaces by default, or any character contained in CHARS.

functions.name: sign
functions.doc: Returns -1, 0 or +1 for negative, zero or positive X. NULL if X is NULL or a string/blob that cannot be losslessly read as a number.

functions.name: soundex
functions.doc: Four-character Soundex code for X ('?000' if X has no letters). Only available when SQLite is compiled with SQLITE_SOUNDEX.

functions.name: sqlite_compileoption_get
functions.doc: Name of the N-th compile-time option used to build this library (0-based), or NULL when N is out of range.

functions.name: sqlite_compileoption_used
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the named compile-time option (the SQLITE_ prefix may be omitted) was used to build the library, else 0.

functions.name: sqlite_offset
functions.doc: Byte offset in the database file of the record holding column X, or NULL if X is not a direct column reference. Requires SQLITE_ENABLE_OFFSET_SQL_FUNC.

functions.name: sqlite_source_id
functions.doc: Identifies the exact source check-in the library was built from: a timestamp followed by the SHA3-256 hash of that check-in.

functions.name: sqlite_version
functions.doc: Version string of the running SQLite library, for example '3.45.1'.

functions.name: substr

signatures.doc: From START to the end of X.
At most LEN characters; negative LEN takes characters before START.

functions.doc: Substring of X starting at the 1-based position START; a negative START counts from the end. For blobs, positions and lengths are in bytes.

functions.name: substring

signatures.doc: From START to the end of X.
At most LEN characters; negative LEN takes characters before START.

functions.doc: Alias of substr(): substring of X from 1-based position START, optionally limited to LEN characters (bytes for blobs).

functions.name: total_changes
functions.doc: Total rows inserted, updated or deleted by completed INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements since this database connection was opened.

functions.name: trim

signatures.doc: Strips spaces from both ends.
Strips any characters in CHARS from both ends.

functions.doc: Removes characters from both ends of X: spaces by default, or any character contained in CHARS.

functions.name: typeof
functions.doc: Storage class of X as a string: 'null', 'integer', 'real', 'text' or 'blob'.

functions.name: unhex

signatures.doc: Characters listed in IGNORE may appear between hex digit pairs.

functions.doc: Decodes the hexadecimal string X into a blob. Returns NULL if X contains an odd number of hex digits or a non-hex character that is not listed in IGNORE.

functions.name: unicode
functions.doc: Unicode code point of the first character of X; the inverse of char().

functions.name: unlikely
functions.doc: Returns X unchanged; a planner hint that X is usually false. Same as likelihood(X, 0.0625).

functions.name: upper
functions.doc: Copy of X with ASCII letters converted to upper case. Non-ASCII case mapping requires the ICU extension.

functions.name: zeroblob
functions.doc: Blob of N zero bytes, stored efficiently. Handy for reserving space that is later filled with incremental blob I/O.

functions.name: avg
functions.doc: Average of the non-NULL values of X in the group, always as a floating-point number; NULL if there are no non-NULL values. Accepts DISTINCT, FILTER and OVER.

functions.name: count

signatures.doc: count(*): number of rows in the group.
Number of rows where X is not NULL.

functions.doc: count(*) counts every row of the group; count(X) counts rows where X is not NULL (count(DISTINCT X) counts distinct non-NULL values).

functions.name: group_concat

signatures.doc: Comma-separated.
Uses SEP as the separator.

functions.doc: Concatenates the non-NULL values of X in the group, separated by SEP (default ','). Order is arbitrary unless an ORDER BY is given inside the call (3.44.0+).

functions.name: string_agg
functions.doc: SQL-standard spelling of group_concat(X, SEP); the separator is required. Supports DISTINCT and an in-call ORDER BY.

functions.name: sum
functions.doc: Sum of non-NULL values: an integer if all inputs are integers, otherwise a float. NULL when there are no non-NULL inputs; raises an error on integer overflow.

functions.name: total
functions.doc: Like sum() but always returns a float, yields 0.0 for an empty group, and never raises an overflow error.

functions.name: row_number
functions.doc: Sequential number of the current row within its partition, starting at 1, following the window's ORDER BY.

functions.name: rank
functions.doc: Rank of the current row with gaps: peers share a rank and the next distinct value skips ahead. Equals row_number() of the first peer.

functions.name: dense_rank
functions.doc: Rank of the current row's peer group without gaps: 1 for the first group, increasing by one per distinct ORDER BY value.

functions.name: percent_rank
functions.doc: Relative rank (rank - 1) / (partition rows - 1), between 0.0 and 1.0; 0.0 for a single-row partition.

functions.name: cume_dist
functions.doc: Cumulative distribution: rows up to and including the current row's last peer, divided by the partition's row count.

functions.name: ntile
functions.doc: Splits the ordered partition into N roughly equal buckets and returns the current row's bucket number, 1 through N.

functions.name: lag
functions.doc: Value of EXPR at OFFSET rows (default 1) before the current row in the partition; DEFAULT (or NULL) when no such row exists.

functions.name: lead
functions.doc: Value of EXPR at OFFSET rows (default 1) after the current row in the partition; DEFAULT (or NULL) when no such row exists.

functions.name: first_value
functions.doc: Value of EXPR evaluated on the first row of the current window frame.

functions.name: last_value
functions.doc: Value of EXPR on the last row of the current window frame. With the default frame this is the current row's last peer, so widen the frame for the partition's last row.

functions.name: nth_value
functions.doc: Value of EXPR on the N-th row (1-based) of the current window frame, or NULL if the frame has fewer than N rows.

functions.name: date

signatures.doc: Current date (UTC).

functions.doc: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Modifiers: 'NNN days|hours|minutes|seconds|months|years', 'start of month|year|day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec'. Time value defaults to 'now'.

functions.name: time

signatures.doc: Current time (UTC).

functions.doc: Time as HH:MM:SS (HH:MM:SS.SSS with 'subsec'). Modifiers: 'NNN days|hours|minutes|seconds|months|years', 'start of month|year|day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec'.

functions.name: datetime

signatures.doc: Current date and time (UTC).

functions.doc: Timestamp as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Modifiers: 'NNN days|hours|minutes|seconds|months|years', 'start of month|year|day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec'.

functions.name: julianday

signatures.doc: Current Julian day number.

functions.doc: Fractional Julian day number. Modifiers: 'NNN days|hours|minutes|seconds|months|years', 'start of month|year|day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec'.

functions.name: unixepoch

signatures.doc: Current Unix time.

functions.doc: Seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC (REAL with 'subsec'). Modifiers: 'NNN days|hours|minutes|seconds|months|years', 'start of month|year|day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec'.

functions.name: strftime

signatures.doc: Modifiers as for date(): 'NNN days|hours|minutes|seconds|months|years', 'start of month|year|day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec'.

functions.doc: Formats a time value. Codes: %Y %m %d %H %M %S, %f (SS.SSS), %s (unix secs), %j (day of year), %J (Julian), %w (0-6, Sun=0), %u (1-7), %W/%V week, %G/%g ISO year, %F %T %R, %e %k %l %I %p %P, %% literal.

functions.name: timediff
functions.doc: Difference as text '(+|-)YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS': the amount of time to add to TIME2 to reach TIME1, expressed in calendar units.

functions.name: current_date
functions.doc: Keyword (written without parentheses) giving the current UTC date as YYYY-MM-DD. Evaluated once per statement.

functions.name: current_time
functions.doc: Keyword (written without parentheses) giving the current UTC time as HH:MM:SS. Evaluated once per statement.

functions.name: current_timestamp
functions.doc: Keyword (written without parentheses) giving the current UTC date and time as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Common as a column DEFAULT.

functions.name: acos
functions.doc: Arccosine of X in radians. Math functions need SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS (on by default in standard builds).

functions.name: acosh
functions.doc: Hyperbolic arccosine of X.

functions.name: asin
functions.doc: Arcsine of X in radians.

functions.name: asinh
functions.doc: Hyperbolic arcsine of X.

functions.name: atan
functions.doc: Arctangent of X in radians.

functions.name: atan2
functions.doc: Arctangent of Y/X in radians, using the signs of both arguments to pick the quadrant (result between -pi and pi).

functions.name: atanh
functions.doc: Hyperbolic arctangent of X.

functions.name: ceil
functions.doc: Smallest integral value not less than X (rounds toward +infinity). Integer input returns an integer, real input a real.

functions.name: ceiling
functions.doc: Alias of ceil(): smallest integral value not less than X.

functions.name: cos
functions.doc: Cosine of X, where X is in radians.

functions.name: cosh
functions.doc: Hyperbolic cosine of X.

functions.name: degrees
functions.doc: Converts X from radians to degrees.

functions.name: exp
functions.doc: e (about 2.71828) raised to the power X.

functions.name: floor
functions.doc: Largest integral value not greater than X (rounds toward -infinity). Integer input returns an integer, real input a real.

functions.name: ln
functions.doc: Natural (base e) logarithm of X.

functions.name: log

signatures.doc: Base-10 logarithm (not natural log).
Logarithm of X in base B.

functions.doc: With one argument, the base-10 logarithm of X (use ln() for natural log). With two, log(B, X) is the logarithm of X in base B.

functions.name: log10
functions.doc: Base-10 logarithm of X.

functions.name: log2
functions.doc: Base-2 logarithm of X.

functions.name: mod
functions.doc: Remainder of X divided by Y. Unlike the % operator it also works on non-integer values.

functions.name: pi
functions.doc: Approximation of the constant pi (3.14159...).

functions.name: pow
functions.doc: X raised to the power Y.

functions.name: power
functions.doc: Alias of pow(): X raised to the power Y.

functions.name: radians
functions.doc: Converts X from degrees to radians.

functions.name: sin
functions.doc: Sine of X, where X is in radians.

functions.name: sinh
functions.doc: Hyperbolic sine of X.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.doc: Square root of X; NULL for negative X.

functions.name: tan
functions.doc: Tangent of X, where X is in radians.

functions.name: tanh
functions.doc: Hyperbolic tangent of X.

functions.name: trunc
functions.doc: Drops the fractional part of X, rounding toward zero.

functions.name: json
functions.doc: Checks that X is valid JSON (text, JSON5 or JSONB) and returns it as minified canonical JSON text; raises an error if X is malformed.

functions.name: jsonb
functions.doc: Parses JSON text (or validates JSONB) in X and returns it in SQLite's binary JSONB format as a blob.

functions.name: json_array
functions.doc: Builds a JSON array from the arguments. Text is quoted as a JSON string unless it came from another JSON function; blobs are an error.

functions.name: jsonb_array
functions.doc: Same as json_array() but returns the array in binary JSONB form.

functions.name: json_array_length

signatures.doc: Length of the array at PATH.

functions.doc: Number of elements in the JSON array (at PATH if given). Returns 0 for a non-array value and NULL if PATH does not exist.

functions.name: json_error_position
functions.doc: Returns 0 if X is well-formed JSON or JSONB; otherwise the 1-based position of the first syntax error (a character offset for text, a byte offset for JSONB).

functions.name: json_extract

signatures.doc: Single path: SQL value, or JSON text for an array/object.
Several paths: JSON array of the results.

functions.doc: Extracts values by path ('$', '$.key', '$[0]', '$[#-1]'). One path gives an SQL value (objects/arrays as JSON text); several paths give a JSON array; a missing path gives NULL.

functions.name: jsonb_extract
functions.doc: Like json_extract() but returns arrays and objects (and multi-path results) as JSONB blobs; scalar values come back as ordinary SQL values.

functions.name: json_insert
functions.doc: Returns JSON with each VALUE added at its PATH only when that path does not already exist; existing values are left alone. '$[#]' appends to an array.

functions.name: jsonb_insert
functions.doc: Same as json_insert() but returns the result as JSONB.

functions.name: json_object
functions.doc: Builds a JSON object from alternating label/value arguments. Labels must be text; values from other JSON functions are embedded as JSON rather than strings.

functions.name: jsonb_object
functions.doc: Same as json_object() but returns the object as JSONB.

functions.name: json_patch
functions.doc: Applies PATCH to TARGET using RFC 7396 MergePatch rules: object members are merged recursively, a null member deletes the key, and non-object patches replace the target.

functions.name: jsonb_patch
functions.doc: Same as json_patch() but returns the result as JSONB.

functions.name: json_pretty

signatures.doc: Uses INDENT for each nesting level.

functions.doc: Returns JSON reformatted with line breaks and indentation for readability; INDENT defaults to four spaces. Added in 3.46.0, so unavailable on older 3.45 builds.

functions.name: json_remove
functions.doc: Returns JSON with the elements at each PATH removed, applied left to right. Paths that do not exist are ignored; with no paths it just minifies.

functions.name: jsonb_remove
functions.doc: Same as json_remove() but returns the result as JSONB.

functions.name: json_replace
functions.doc: Returns JSON with values at existing PATHs overwritten by the matching VALUE; paths that do not exist are not created.

functions.name: jsonb_replace
functions.doc: Same as json_replace() but returns the result as JSONB.

functions.name: json_set
functions.doc: Returns JSON with each VALUE written at its PATH, overwriting existing values and creating missing ones (an upsert of json_insert and json_replace).

functions.name: jsonb_set
functions.doc: Same as json_set() but returns the result as JSONB.

functions.name: json_type

signatures.doc: Type of the element at PATH.

functions.doc: JSON type of the value (at PATH if given): 'null', 'true', 'false', 'integer', 'real', 'text', 'array' or 'object'. NULL if PATH does not exist.

functions.name: json_valid

signatures.doc: 3.45.0+: bit flags 1=RFC 8259 text, 2=JSON5 text, 4=JSONB (quick check), 8=JSONB (strict).

functions.doc: Returns 1 if X is well-formed JSON, else 0 (NULL for NULL). Without FLAGS only canonical RFC 8259 text counts as valid.

functions.name: json_quote
functions.doc: Converts an SQL value to its JSON representation: numbers stay numbers, text becomes a quoted JSON string, NULL becomes null. JSON from another JSON function passes through.

functions.name: json_group_array
functions.doc: Aggregate that collects every X in the group (NULLs included as null) into a single JSON array.

functions.name: jsonb_group_array
functions.doc: Same as json_group_array() but returns the array as JSONB.

functions.name: json_group_object
functions.doc: Aggregate that builds a JSON object from the group, using NAME as each key and VALUE as its value.

functions.name: jsonb_group_object
functions.doc: Same as json_group_object() but returns the object as JSONB.

functions.name: json_each
functions.doc: Table-valued: one row per direct child of the top-level array/object (or the element at PATH). Columns: key, value, type, atom, id, parent, fullkey, path; hidden json, root.

functions.name: json_tree
functions.doc: Table-valued: walks the JSON recursively, one row per element including the root (or from PATH). Columns: key, value, type, atom, id, parent, fullkey, path; hidden json, root.

functions.name: bm25
functions.doc: FTS5 auxiliary function: BM25 relevance of the current match, optionally weighting each column. Lower (more negative) means a better match, so ORDER BY it ascending; 'rank' uses it by default.

functions.name: highlight
functions.doc: FTS5 auxiliary function: full text of column COL (0-based) of the matched row, with each matched phrase wrapped in OPEN and CLOSE markers.

functions.name: snippet
functions.doc: FTS5 auxiliary function: short excerpt (up to TOKENS, 1-64) around matches, matches wrapped in OPEN/CLOSE and ELLIPSIS marking cut text. COL -1 lets FTS5 pick the best column.

functions.name: generate_series
functions.doc: Table-valued integer sequence from START to STOP by STEP (default 1). Column: value; hidden start, stop, step. Provided by the series extension (built into the sqlite3 CLI), not the core library.

functions.name: pragma_table_info
functions.doc: One row per visible column of TABLE. Columns: cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk (1-based position in the primary key, 0 if not part of it).

functions.name: pragma_table_xinfo
functions.doc: Like pragma_table_info but also lists hidden and generated columns. Columns: cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk, hidden (0 normal, 1 hidden, 2 virtual generated, 3 stored generated).

functions.name: pragma_table_list
functions.doc: Tables and views in the attached schemas. Columns: schema, name, type ('table', 'view', 'virtual', 'shadow'), ncol, wr (WITHOUT ROWID flag), strict.

functions.name: pragma_index_list
functions.doc: Indexes on TABLE. Columns: seq, name, unique, origin ('c' CREATE INDEX, 'u' UNIQUE constraint, 'pk' primary key), partial.

functions.name: pragma_index_info
functions.doc: Key columns of the named index. Columns: seqno (rank within index), cid (table column, -1 rowid, -2 expression), name (NULL for expressions).

functions.name: pragma_index_xinfo
functions.doc: All columns stored in the index, including auxiliary ones. Columns: seqno, cid, name, desc (1 if DESC), coll (collation), key (1 for key columns, 0 for auxiliary).

functions.name: pragma_foreign_key_list
functions.doc: Foreign keys declared on TABLE, one row per column pair. Columns: id, seq, table (parent), from, to, on_update, on_delete, match.

functions.name: pragma_database_list
functions.doc: Databases attached to the connection. Columns: seq, name ('main', 'temp' or the ATTACH alias), file (path, empty for in-memory/temp).

functions.name: pragma_function_list
functions.doc: SQL functions known to the connection. Columns: name, builtin (1 if built in), type ('s' scalar, 'a' aggregate, 'w' window), enc, narg (-1 variadic), flags.

functions.name: pragma_collation_list
functions.doc: Collating sequences registered on the connection. Columns: seq, name.

functions.name: pragma_module_list
functions.doc: Virtual table modules registered on the connection (e.g. fts5, rtree, json_each). Column: name.

functions.name: pragma_pragma_list
functions.doc: Names of the PRAGMA commands supported by this build. Column: name.

operators.doc: JSON extract (3.38.0+): X->P returns the JSON text representation of the element at P. P may be a path like '$.a[0]', a bare object label, or an integer array index. NULL if missing.
JSON extract (3.38.0+): X->>P returns the element at P as an SQL value (TEXT, INTEGER, REAL or NULL) rather than JSON. Same path forms as ->.
String concatenation of the text forms of both operands. The result is NULL if either operand is NULL; use concat() to skip NULLs.
Pattern match: % matches any run of characters, _ exactly one. ASCII case-insensitive by default; supports an ESCAPE clause and NOT LIKE.
Case-sensitive Unix-style pattern match with * (any run), ? (one character) and [...] character classes. S GLOB P calls glob(P, S).
X REGEXP Y calls a user-supplied regexp(Y, X) function; core SQLite defines none, so it errors unless an extension (such as the CLI's regexp) provides it.
Full-text search predicate for FTS3/FTS4/FTS5 tables (e.g. tbl MATCH 'query'). Elsewhere it calls a user-defined match() function and errors if none exists.
Equality test that treats NULLs as comparable: NULL IS NULL is true and the result is never NULL.
Inequality counterpart of IS: true when operands differ, treating NULL as an ordinary value; never returns NULL.
SQL-standard synonym for IS NOT (3.39.0+): true when the operands differ, with NULLs compared as values.
SQL-standard synonym for IS (3.39.0+): true when the operands are equal or both NULL.
X BETWEEN Y AND Z is equivalent to X >= Y AND X <= Z, with X evaluated once. NOT BETWEEN negates it.
X IN (list or subquery) is true if X equals any member; NULL if not found and the list contains NULL. NOT IN negates it.
Postfix operator selecting the collating sequence for comparisons and sorting, e.g. name COLLATE NOCASE. Built-ins: BINARY, NOCASE, RTRIM.
